scope: Design-only review of frozen grok-implementation-revision-02 (DESIGN, TRIGGER, GROK-WORKER-PROMPT, REVIEW-PROMPTS, SOURCES, ALL-DOCS-READING, CORRECTIONS, help snapshots, CLI identity and 1.0.25 smoke receipts), plus startup routing (AGENTS.md, ACTIVE-ROUTING.md, the 2026-09-10 assignment, develop SKILL.md) and the preserved original DESIGN items 1–19. The review covers source fidelity, reading-coverage honesty, model identities, permission and CLI/API limitations, the absence of a new scheduler, normative original gates, independent audits, descendant quiescence, recovery binding and disposition of revision-01 findings. Excluded: any product launch, runtime control verification, product/roadmap acceptance, and the other fresh revision-02 reviewer's verdict (not read). This verdict cannot waive the unperformed mandatory pre-dispatch control gate.
summary: Revision 02 correctly fixes the revision-01 requested changes. Specifically: dontAsk is no longer described as a closed allowlist; Bash prefix and env/wrapper stripping are admitted; both help snapshots are preserved; the 1.0.25 binary is pinned with an unchanged before/after hash; --verbatim is restored; original items 1–19 are made normative with the correct SHA; recovery via ACTIVE-ROUTING and the assignment is specified; descendant cleanup before freeze is required; and per-tool identity is not inferred from outcomes. The product-launch gate is clearly fail-closed and specified-only. It correctly rejects a positive fixture or a bare --sandbox flag as proof. One blocking gap remains. The gate binds and contains the launched client process, but shipped docs indicate model and tool execution may run in a shared Grok leader outside that process tree. As specified, the binary pin, quiescence check and child-secret negative control could therefore give false assurance. The repair is a small addition to the existing receipt and quiescence text, not a new framework.

findings.path: deliverables/roadmap-loop-2026-09-10/grok-implementation-revision-02/DESIGN.md (Concrete installed CLI contract: sanitized launch receipt, mandatory negative-control paragraph, and pre-freeze descendant paragraph); TRIGGER.txt launch paragraph
findings.requirement: Three requirements depend on binding the actual executor. (1) The binary/version/hash recorded before and after must identify what actually runs the worker. (2) Descendant quiescence before freeze must be verified through the existing supervisor, process group or cgroup. (3) The child-process secret/network negative controls must reflect the environment real tool children inherit.
findings.consequence: The pinned shipped sandbox guide (revision-01 raw/local-18-sandbox.md, 'How It Works') says that when a non-off sandbox is requested 'the agent runs in-process, not through the shared leader, so tool calls stay in this process', and that a note appears 'if leader mode would otherwise have been on'. Current help exposes --leader-socket (default ~/.grok/leader.sock) and `grok leader` management. So without an enforced sandbox, a headless run may delegate the agent and its run_terminal_cmd children to a pre-existing shared leader. If that happens: (a) hashing /home/charl/.grok/bin/grok-1.0.25 before and after does not bind the process executing model or tool calls, which could be an older or different leader binary; (b) tool children, including backgrounded jobs, are descendants of the leader, outside the launched process group or cgroup, so group termination and cgroup limits neither contain nor stop them, and owned paths can change after hashes are frozen for reviewers; (c) a harmless fixture secret placed in the launch environment would be absent from leader-spawned children, so the env-secret negative check would 'pass' while the leader's real inherited environment stays exposed. The 1.0.25 smoke receipt records only the client PID and empty stderr, so it cannot tell whether a leader was used. This is an inference from shipped docs and help, not an observed runtime fact. The design neither resolves it nor lists it as a receipt field.
findings.repair: In the existing DESIGN receipt and quiescence text, add the following. The sanitized launch receipt records the actual executor mode (in-process or leader), leader socket, leader PID, executable path/version/hash and cgroup, observed before and after. Tool-call child PIDs must be observed as descendants of the supervised pinned process, or of a dedicated leader started from the same pinned binary under the same supervision via the existing --leader-socket option. Negative-control fixtures are placed in the actual executor's environment. If executor binding or descendancy cannot be shown, that dispatch fails closed. Optionally add 'bind actual executor/leader' to the TRIGGER launch clause. No new scheduler, runner or permission framework is needed.

findings.path: DESIGN.md sanitized launch receipt ('loaded rule/hook sources, trust requirement, inherited and remembered grants')
findings.requirement: Inspect effective merged permission configuration before launch.
findings.consequence: Pinned local-12-project-rules.md and local-22-permissions-and-safety.md state that Grok merges ~/.claude/settings.json and settings.local.json permission rules, ~/.claude/rules, ~/.claude/CLAUDE*.md and ~/.cursor sources through default-on compatibility. Home-level sources are not gated by folder trust, and this host also runs the Claude CLI. The receipt wording is generic, so a root operator could inspect only ~/.grok and the checkout and miss an inherited broad allow such as Bash(*). Local docs also name a --trust flag that is absent from current 1.0.25 help, so trust behavior must be observed, not assumed.
findings.repair: Name the Claude/Cursor compatibility home and project sources in the receipt. Retain sanitized `grok inspect` output from the actual --cwd, and record the observed trust state. No configuration change is required.

findings.requirement: No new scheduler; admitted tools only.
findings.consequence: Headless docs say --tools 'preserves the selected agent profile's injection policy' and MCP meta-tools remain unless denied. The background-tasks guide documents scheduler_create (including durable), monitor and background shell tools. The design never records the effective tool list, so the absence of scheduler, monitor or unexpected tools is assumed rather than observed.
findings.repair: Retain the actually advertised tool list in the launch receipt, for example the streaming-json available_commands event or equivalent, and fail closed if scheduler, monitor or unadmitted tools are present.

findings.requirement: Honest feasibility of the shell route without global configuration changes.
findings.consequence: Shipped sandbox docs make [shell_environment_policy] default to inherit=all with default excludes ignored, and describe it as a config setting. The project rules guide says non-MCP/plugin/permission settings load only from ~/.grok/config.toml. Because the design forbids changing global configuration, the admitted shell route will likely fail the child-secret gate unless an existing policy is already in place. The source-only/no-shell route is then the realistic default, but the design does not say so.
findings.repair: State that, absent pre-existing effective env filtering observed in the receipt, root uses the source-only route and runs checks separately.

findings.path: SOURCES.md 'Local CLI observations'; CORRECTIONS.md version row
findings.consequence: The only pinned version capture, revision-01 raw/grok-version.txt, reads 'grok 1.0.25 (f7e67d6988e2)'. Revision-01 raw/grok-help.txt is byte-identical (8dd784…) to current-help-1.0.25.txt. The '1.0.13 (5e9a58528b76)' observation has no pinned artifact in the manifest. SOURCES cites the revision-01 'Captured help' as if historical, but it is current help. Conclusions are unaffected because the design pins 1.0.25 and treats historical canaries as unbound, but provenance is blurred.
findings.repair: Label 1.0.13 as parent-reported and unpinned, or cite its artifact. Note that revision-01's own raw captures are already 1.0.25.

findings.path: REVIEW-PROMPTS.md and SOURCES.md (absolute link to .worktrees/sp03-expression-k-macro05/.../opus-review.json); DESIGN.md ('checkpoint routing fact 374', /tmp/moriarty-sp05-next-terra-followup.md); CORRECTIONS.md (review-01 verdict files)
findings.requirement: Hash-pinned evidence for cited claims and recovery inputs.
findings.consequence: Several items are cited as evidence or recovery inputs but are not in the candidate manifest: the PASS_SCOPED 189.118 s Opus receipt, checkpoint fact 374, the /tmp task input and the review-01 verdicts. They cannot be independently verified from the frozen candidate. A /tmp input may also disappear across host restarts.
findings.repair: Add hashes to the manifest, or mark these items explicitly as root-reported and unpinned. Before relying on the /tmp task input, copy it into existing task records and record its hash.

findings.path: DESIGN.md 'Review and continuation' (two-vote authority 'with the current participating models')
findings.requirement: Original item 11 majority-vote authority, now under changed routing.
findings.consequence: Original item 11 names 'GPT-6/Grok' voters. Under new routing, Grok is the author, so 'current participating models' could be read as letting the author vote on design or resource amendments to its own slice.
findings.repair: Name the voting identities, for example non-author Opus and Astra, or state whether an author vote counts.

findings.path: SOURCES.md closing sections and applicable-document table
findings.requirement: Internal consistency of the frozen text.
findings.consequence: Three stale phrases remain. 'Revision 02 applies CORRECTIONS.md from the fresh independent Astra review' omits the Opus findings. 'Current binary/tool smoke evidence must be inspected before final freeze' contradicts the frozen status. Table rows saying 'applicable guide inspected' sit beside the full-reading claim. The prose does explain the table, so the claims are not wrong, only inconsistent.
findings.repair: Edit the wording in a successor revision; no substantive change.

findings.path: AGENTS.md ('Current implementation and review routing', 'Autonomous sprint decisions', 'Development plugin' paragraph); plugins/moriarty-dev/skills/develop/SKILL.md 'Product Routing' and workflow line
findings.consequence: The AGENTS.md override section does supersede 'older model routing below', and SKILL.md defers to later user steering, so recovery is adequately bound. However, loaded startup text still says GPT-6 implements, Astra and Grok review, and the September 9 update 'replaces Opus for pending and future reviews'. ACTIVE-ROUTING.md does not yet record a revision or hash, which is expected before adoption. This leaves a misreading risk after compaction.
findings.repair: After adoption, update ACTIVE-ROUTING with the accepted manifest hash, as DESIGN already requires. Reconcile the stale routing sentences as an ordinary authorized documentation edit. Not required for design approval.

checks: Cross-checked every design-artifacts-manifest file hash against the candidate manifest entries: SOURCES, DESIGN, TRIGGER, worker, review, ALL-DOCS, inventory, CORRECTIONS, help manifest, both help files, CLI identity, both smoke receipts, AGENTS, ACTIVE-ROUTING and the assignment. All match textually. I did not compute SHA-256 over the supplied bytes; root verification is relied upon.

Confirmed originalDesignSha256 3ec27f7c… in DESIGN.md and the manifest matches the pinned original DESIGN.md, and original items 1–19 are declared normative except for routing and first-task selection.
TRIGGER.txt: manifest triggerCharacters 3966 against 3974 bytes is consistent with four en dashes (2 extra bytes each). It is under the 4,000-character limit.

Permission claims checked against pinned local-22 and local-14: dontAsk still allows built-in read-only tools and shell commands; remembered grants apply outside always-approve; Bash prefix matching has no word boundary; env assignments and wrappers are stripped; allow rules are conjunctive and not a closed allowlist; deny beats allow, so a catch-all Bash deny defeats allowlisting; Read deny also governs grep and shell file operands; ~/ is literal in patterns; hooks fail open; --tools keeps MCP meta-tools. DESIGN wording is faithful.

Sandbox claims checked against local-18: built-in profile setup failure continues unenforced; child network blocking is Linux seccomp only; in-process tools and the API are unaffected. DESIGN's 'strict alone cannot satisfy the gate' is faithful. The same file is the source of the leader-delegation concern in R2-OPUS-1.

Worktree correction: raw/parent-earlier-help.txt contains 'Headless (-p) does not create a worktree from this flag'. current-help-1.0.25.txt omits it. The local-14 headless doc describes creation including dirty changes. The design uses a pre-created checkout via --cwd and makes no untested automatic-worktree claim.
--no-auto-update: listed in the installed headless doc but absent from current 1.0.25 help. DESIGN correctly declines to add it blindly.

Model identity: the Grok receipts show requested grok-4.6 returning modelUsage key grok-4.6-build, and the design does not claim checkpoint equivalence. The Opus canary shows requested 'opus' returning canonicalModel claude-opus-5/firstParty, which is pinned for reviews, with per-review returned-identity verification required.

1.0.25 smoke receipt: versioned executable, binaryHashUnchanged true, exit 0, end_turn, 4 turns, 53.831 s, and a scope disclaimer that it does not prove tool events or secret/network confinement. This matches the DESIGN and SOURCES claims.

Reading coverage: ALL-DOCS-READING records 181 sections in 190 chunks, the full 42-page card (pages 0–41), eight heading-only gRPC sections and empty voice/connector fields explicitly unreviewed, and no reread claimed in revision 02. This is consistent with the revision-01 manifest already containing the same inventory hash 13e4a8…. The model-card text excerpt is consistent with the cited 31.9% SWE-Marathon, 1.7% hallucination and high-stakes oversight statements.

No new scheduler: the design excludes Grok /loop, daemons, timers and new harnesses, and reuses the existing native goal without recreation or false completion. This is consistent with the assignment and AGENTS.md.

Independent audits: REVIEW-PROMPTS requires two fresh non-author reviewers (claude-opus-5 medium, gpt-6-astra medium), no shared initial opinions, exact candidate hashes, and no approval from exit zero, plan fragments, timeout or unavailability. Both approvals are required and neither substitutes for product, resource or network acceptance.

Descendant quiescence: DESIGN and the worker prompt require terminating residual descendants, rechecking owned-path hashes after quiescence, and refusing to freeze otherwise. The mechanism is sound for in-tree children but does not cover leader-hosted children (R2-OPUS-1).

Gate clarity: DESIGN, REVIEW-PROMPTS, CORRECTIONS and SOURCES consistently state that the mandatory pre-dispatch controls are specified-only, not satisfied by the positive fixture, a READY canary, a sandbox flag or this design verdict, and fail closed for the affected dispatch.

SP05 worker predicate: the systemd fields (MainPID=0, Result=success, ExecMainCode=1 i.e. CLD_EXITED, ExecMainStatus=0, matching InvocationID, pre-stop capture, rejection of not-found/default/post-stop reads) are internally coherent. FINANCIAL_COMPLETE is explicitly not exit zero, and historical missing-exit evidence is preserved.
gateAssessment: The product-launch gate is clear, correctly specified-only and fail-closed. It is sufficient except that it binds the launched client rather than the actual executor. Add the leader/executor binding (R2-OPUS-1); recording the effective toolset and compatibility sources (R2-OPUS-2/3) is recommended. No product launch is required to review this design, and none is authorized by this verdict.
limitations: No-tools review: I executed no commands, computed no hashes, and inspected only the supplied packet text.

Not reproduced in the packet, so not personally inspected: raw/all-docs.md corpus, both inventory JSONs, model-card.pdf, local-05-configuration, local-10-hooks, local-17-sessions, local-19-plan-mode, local-24-monitoring-usage, local-26-config-reference, the first native-JSON canary, opus-availability.json, revision-01 DESIGN/TRIGGER/worker/review/SOURCES/ALL-DOCS bodies, and the revision-01 Astra/Opus review verdicts. Dispositions in CORRECTIONS were judged against revision-02 text, not the original finding wording.

The leader-delegation concern (R2-OPUS-1) is inferred from shipped sandbox docs and help. Whether headless 1.0.25 on this host actually uses a shared leader is unverified. The config reference that may define leader defaults was not supplied.
The Opus K PASS_SCOPED receipt, checkpoint fact 374, the /tmp task input and the review-01 files are cited but unpinned and were not inspected.
Effective host configuration, trust, remembered grants, hooks, sandbox availability on WSL2, network endpoints and supervisor/cgroup mechanisms are runtime facts outside this design review.
I did not read the other fresh revision-02 reviewer's verdict and did not share opinions.

claims: No product, roadmap, sprint, proof, Preview or launch-control completion is claimed. Design approval is withheld pending R2-OPUS-1. Even after approval, product dispatch remains blocked until the actual checkout/control negative tests and sanitized current configuration receipts exist.
